types.embedding_query_text: Person: A human being. Also called Individual, Human, Man, Woman, Chef. Examples: Benoît Castel, Nina Métayer, Romain Montbabut, Hélène Darroze.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Person' directly matches schema.org's 'Person' class, which describes an individual human being.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: MemberProgramTier
candidates.comment: An intangible representing a specific tier within a loyalty or membership program. Also called membership level, loyalty tier, program status. Examples: "Gold Member", "Platinum Tier", "Basic Membership Level".

candidates.label: MenuItem
candidates.comment: An intangible representing a single food or drink item listed within a menu or menu section. Also called menu item, dish, beverage. Examples: "Spaghetti Carbonara", "Caesar Salad", "Coca-Cola", "Chocolate Lava Cake". Distinct from Menu, which is the entire list.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: Thing
candidates.comment: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.

types.embedding_query_text: City: A large and densely populated urban area. Also called Metropolis, Town, Urban center, Municipality. Examples: Paris, Singapore.

chosen_type.label: City
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'City' directly matches schema.org's 'City' class, which describes a large human settlement.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: Zoo
candidates.comment: A civic structure and facility where wild animals are housed, exhibited, and often bred for conservation and public education. Also called zoological garden, animal park, wildlife park. Examples: San Diego Zoo, London Zoo, Bronx Zoo.

candidates.label: CityHall
candidates.comment: A government building serving as the administrative headquarters for a city or town. Also called town hall, municipal building, civic center. Examples: New York City Hall, London City Hall, a local town's municipal office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

candidates.label: SubwayStation
candidates.comment: A civic structure serving as a stop or terminal for subway or metro trains. Also called metro station, underground station, tube station. Examples: 'Grand Central Terminal', 'London Underground station', 'Tokyo Metro station'.

types.embedding_query_text: Organization: A structured group of people with a particular purpose. Also called Association, Institution, Society, Body, Union. Examples: International Union of Bakers and Confectioners, UIBC.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Organization' directly matches schema.org's 'Organization' class, which describes a group of people with a purpose.

mentions: International Union of Bakers and Confectioners

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

candidates.label: WorkersUnion
candidates.comment: An organization that advocates for the interests of its worker members through collective bargaining and political lobbying. Also called labor union, trade union, industrial union. Examples: United Auto Workers (UAW), National Education Association (NEA), a local plumbers' union.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

types.embedding_query_text: Award: A prize or other mark of recognition given in honor of an achievement. Also called Prize, Honor, Recognition, Trophy, Accolade. Examples: World Confectioner of the Year.

chosen_type.label: Award
chosen_type.definition: A prize or honor bestowed for an achievement.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents an 'Award' as an entity; existing candidates are actions or events. Minting 'Award' as a new type under 'Thing' is appropriate.

candidates.label: WinAction
candidates.comment: The act of achieving victory or success in a competitive activity. Also called triumph, succeed, prevail. Examples: winning a race, winning a championship, winning an argument.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: ConferenceEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

candidates.label: DeliveryEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing the delivery of an item, typically a product or package. Also called Shipping event, package delivery, consignment event. Examples: A package arriving at its destination, a food delivery being completed, a furniture delivery appointment. Distinct from Order, which is the request for items, not the delivery itself.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

types.embedding_query_text: Date: A particular day, month, or year. Also called Day, Month, Year, Period, Time. Examples: last month, three years after, July 14, 2012.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Date' aligns with schema.org's 'Date' datatype, representing specific calendar days, months, or years.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

types.embedding_query_text: Region: An area or division, especially part of a country or the world having definable characteristics but not always fixed boundaries. Also called Area, District, Territory, Zone, Province. Examples: Brittany, US Pacific Northwest, western France, his home region.

chosen_type.label: DefinedRegion
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Region' fits 'DefinedRegion' which describes geographic areas with potentially non-administrative criteria, covering both 'Brittany' and 'US Pacific Northwest'.

candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: SchoolDistrict
candidates.comment: An administrative area responsible for the organization and operation of public schools within its geographical boundaries. Also called education district, school system, local education authority. Examples: 'Los Angeles Unified School District', 'New York City Department of Education', 'Springfield School District 186'.

types.embedding_query_text: Country: A nation or territory considered as an organized political community under one government. Also called Nation, State, Land, Realm, Commonwealth. Examples: France.

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Country' directly matches schema.org's 'Country' class, which describes a sovereign state or nation.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: Embassy
candidates.comment: An Embassy is a GovernmentBuilding representing the diplomatic mission of one country in another. Also called consulate, diplomatic mission, high commission. Examples: The U.S. Embassy in London, the French Embassy in Washington D.C., a country's consulate general.

candidates.label: PoliticalParty
candidates.comment: A PoliticalParty is an Organization formed to contest elections and hold power in government. Also called political movement, party. Examples: Democratic Party, Republican Party, Labour Party, Conservative Party.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

types.embedding_query_text: Pastry: A dough of flour, water, and shortening, and often eggs, that is baked and used in pies and other dishes. Also called Baked good, Confectionery, Dessert, Sweet, Cake. Examples: blueberry and raspberry tartlets, cherry clafoutis, vanilla flans, chocolate choux pastry.

chosen_type.label: Pastry
chosen_type.definition: A baked food item made from dough, often sweet.
chosen_type.justification: None of the schema.org candidates represent a food item like 'Pastry'; they are all types of establishments. Minting 'Pastry' as a new type under 'Product' is appropriate.

candidates.label: Bakery
candidates.comment: A FoodEstablishment that bakes and sells bread, cakes, and pastries. Also called bake shop, patisserie, bread shop. Examples: "The Daily Bread Bakery", "Sweet Delights Patisserie", "Grandma's Oven".

candidates.label: CafeOrCoffeeShop
candidates.comment: A CafeOrCoffeeShop is a FoodEstablishment primarily serving coffee, other beverages, and often light meals or pastries. Also called coffee house, coffee bar, cafe. Examples: Starbucks, local independent coffee shop, a small bistro. Distinct from Restaurant, which typically offers a wider range of full meals.

candidates.label: Distillery
candidates.comment: A Distillery is a FoodEstablishment that produces alcoholic beverages through distillation. Also called liquor producer, spirits manufacturer, alcohol plant. Examples: Jack Daniel's Distillery, The Macallan Distillery, Absolut Vodka Distillery. Distinct from Brewery, which produces beer through fermentation.

candidates.label: IceCreamShop
candidates.comment: An IceCreamShop is a food establishment local business specializing in selling ice cream and related frozen desserts. Also called gelateria, ice cream parlor, frozen dessert shop. Examples: Baskin-Robbins, Ben & Jerry's Scoop Shop, a local artisanal ice cream store.

candidates.label: BarOrPub
candidates.comment: A FoodEstablishment that primarily serves alcoholic beverages and often food. Also called bar, pub, tavern, lounge. Examples: "The Green Dragon Pub", "O'Malley's Bar & Grill", "The Corner Taproom". Distinct from Restaurant, which primarily focuses on serving meals.

types.embedding_query_text: FoodItem: Any substance consumed to provide nutritional support for an organism. Also called Food, Edible, Provision, Ingredient, Produce. Examples: small, scalloped shortbread biscuit, Fruit and vegetables, butter, previous day's unsold stock.

chosen_type.label: FoodItem
chosen_type.definition: Any substance consumed for nutritional support.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class broadly covers 'FoodItem' for both prepared food and raw ingredients without implying a menu or specific use. Minting 'FoodItem' under 'Product' is the best fit.

candidates.label: DietarySupplement
candidates.comment: A product taken orally that contains dietary ingredients intended to supplement the diet, such as vitamins, minerals, or herbs. Also called Nutritional supplement, health supplement, vitamin, herbal remedy. Examples: Multivitamin pills, fish oil capsules, protein powder, ginseng extract. Distinct from Drug, which is primarily for treating, preventing, or diagnosing disease.

candidates.label: MenuItem
candidates.comment: An intangible representing a single food or drink item listed within a menu or menu section. Also called menu item, dish, beverage. Examples: "Spaghetti Carbonara", "Caesar Salad", "Coca-Cola", "Chocolate Lava Cake". Distinct from Menu, which is the entire list.

candidates.label: HowToSupply
candidates.comment: A HowToSupply is a HowToItem that is consumed or used up when performing the instructions for how to achieve a result. Also called consumable item, ingredient, material. Examples: flour, sugar, paint, batteries. Distinct from HowToTool, which is used but not consumed.

candidates.label: DataFeedItem
candidates.comment: A DataFeedItem is an individual entry or record contained within a larger DataFeed. Also called feed entry, feed item, data record. Examples: A single news article in an RSS feed, one product listing in an inventory feed, a single weather observation in a data stream.

candidates.label: FoodService
candidates.comment: A FoodService is a Service related to providing food, such as breakfast, lunch, or dinner. Also called meal service, catering service, dining option. Examples: Breakfast service at a hotel, a school lunch program, an in-flight meal service, a catering package for an event.

types.embedding_query_text: Location: A particular place or position. Also called Place, Site, Spot, Area, Venue. Examples: vegetable gardens and orchards, his own vegetable gardens and orchards.

chosen_type.label: Place
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Location' is best represented by schema.org's 'Place', which describes an entity with a fixed physical extension.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.

types.embedding_query_text: Occupation: A job or profession. Also called Profession, Job, Career, Vocation, Trade. Examples: farmers, artists, cook, gardener.

chosen_type.label: Occupation
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Occupation' directly matches schema.org's 'Occupation' class, which describes a job or profession.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

candidates.label: Attorney
candidates.comment: An Attorney is a LegalService professional who practices law, providing legal advice and representation. Also called lawyer, legal counsel, barrister, solicitor. Examples: a criminal defense attorney, a corporate lawyer, a family law solicitor, a public defender. Distinct from LegalService, which is the broader category of services provided by legal professionals.

candidates.label: ProfessionalService
candidates.comment: ProfessionalService is a LocalBusiness type for providers of specialized services. Also called expert service, specialized service. Examples: a legal service, an accounting service, a dental practice, an architectural firm. Distinct from Service, which is a broader concept of an intangible offering.

candidates.label: HousePainter
candidates.comment: A HousePainter is a home and construction local business providing painting services for houses and other structures. Also called painting contractor, residential painter, decorator. Examples: a local exterior painting service, an interior decorator, a commercial painting company.

candidates.label: SoftwareApplication
candidates.comment: A computer program designed to perform specific tasks for a user. Also called application, app, computer program, software. Examples: Microsoft Word, Adobe Photoshop, a mobile game, a web browser.

types.embedding_query_text: FamilyRelation: The connection between individuals by blood, marriage, or adoption. Also called Relative, Kin, Family member, Relation. Examples: grandparents, mother, grandmother.

chosen_type.label: FamilyRelation
chosen_type.definition: A connection between individuals by blood, marriage, or adoption.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class represents 'FamilyRelation' as an entity; existing candidates are places, audiences, or actions. Minting 'FamilyRelation' as a new type under 'Thing' is appropriate.

candidates.label: SingleFamilyResidence
candidates.comment: A type of house designed to be occupied by one family, typically detached from other homes. Also called detached house, single-family home, private residence. Examples: a suburban house with a yard, a standalone cottage, a bungalow.

candidates.label: ParentAudience
candidates.comment: A ParentAudience, as a PeopleAudience, describes characteristics of parents who might be interested in certain content. Also called parental demographic, parent group, family audience. Examples: 'parents of young children', 'parents of teenagers', 'expectant parents'. Distinct from PeopleAudience, which is a broader category for any group of people.

candidates.label: Gene
candidates.comment: A Gene is a BioChemEntity representing a discrete unit of inheritance that affects one or more biological traits. Also called genetic unit, hereditary factor. Examples: FOXP2, SCARNA21, the gene for eye color, a specific allele.

candidates.label: UserCheckins
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of checking into a location or event. Also called user check-in, location check-in, event attendance. Examples: a user checking into a restaurant, checking into a concert, marking attendance at a conference.

candidates.label: MarryAction
candidates.comment: The act of entering into marriage with another person. Also called get married, wed, tie the knot. Examples: a wedding ceremony, a civil marriage, eloping.

types.embedding_query_text: Age: The length of time that a person has lived or a thing has existed. Also called Years old, Maturity, Period of life, Stage of life. Examples: age of seven, three years later, 54-year-old.

chosen_type.label: Duration
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Age' refers to a length of time, which is best represented by schema.org's 'Duration' datatype.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: AdultOrientedEnumeration
candidates.comment: AdultOrientedEnumeration is an Enumeration of factors that make a product or content relevant or potentially restricted for adults only. Also called adult content classification, age restriction type, mature content indicator. Examples: `AdultSexualContent`, `ViolentContent`, `GamblingContent`.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: ShippingDeliveryTime
candidates.comment: A structured value providing details about the expected delivery times for product shipping. Also called delivery timeframe, estimated delivery, shipping lead time, transit time. Examples: 'ships in 1-2 business days', 'delivery by Friday', 'estimated 3-5 day transit'.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

types.embedding_query_text: Publication: A book, journal, or other printed or electronic work. Also called Book, Document, Work, Text, Writing. Examples: first recipe book.

chosen_type.label: Book
chosen_type.justification: The mention 'first recipe book' is a specific instance of a 'Book', which is a creative work.

candidates.label: Book
candidates.comment: A CreativeWork consisting of a written or printed work, typically bound together and protected by a cover. Also called publication, volume, printed matter. Examples: "To Kill a Mockingbird", "The Lord of the Rings", "A textbook on physics". Distinct from BookSeries, which is a collection of books.

candidates.label: PublicationIssue
candidates.comment: A PublicationIssue is a CreativeWork representing a part of a successively published periodical or publication volume, often numbered and containing a grouping of works. Also called journal issue, magazine issue, periodical issue. Examples: "Nature" Vol. 500, Issue 1; "The New Yorker" October 26, 2023 issue; a specific issue of a scientific journal. Distinct from PublicationVolume, which is a larger grouping of issues.

candidates.label: PublicationVolume
candidates.comment: A PublicationVolume is a CreativeWork representing a part of a successively published periodical or multi-volume work, often numbered and potentially spanning a time period. Also called journal volume, book volume, periodical volume. Examples: "Nature" Volume 500; "Encyclopedia Britannica" Volume 1; a year's collection of a magazine. Distinct from PublicationIssue, which is a smaller, more granular part of a volume.

candidates.label: PublicationEvent
candidates.comment: A PublicationEvent is an Event corresponding to the publication of a CreativeWork, regardless of its type or delivery medium. Also called release event, publishing event. Examples: the release of a new book, the broadcast of a TV show, the online publication of an article, the launch of a new album.

candidates.label: Manuscript
candidates.comment: A creative work, such as a book, document, or musical piece, written by hand rather than typed or printed. Also called handwritten document, original script, autograph. Examples: a medieval illuminated manuscript, an author's handwritten draft of a novel, a composer's original musical score.

types.embedding_query_text: Landmark: An object or feature of a landscape or town that is easily seen and recognized. Also called Monument, Feature, Site, Structure, Icon. Examples: Loire valley Château de Chambord, Château de Chambord.

chosen_type.label: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Landmark' is best represented by schema.org's 'LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings', which specifically covers important historical sites.

candidates.label: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings
candidates.comment: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings is a place representing an important historical landmark or building. Also called historical site, heritage building, monument. Examples: Eiffel Tower, Colosseum, Statue of Liberty, a historic courthouse.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

candidates.label: TouristDestination
candidates.comment: A place, region, or area that is a primary focus for tourism, often containing multiple tourist attractions. Also called travel destination, vacation spot, tourist region. Examples: Paris, the Grand Canyon, the Caribbean islands, a specific resort town. Distinct from TouristAttraction, which is a specific point of interest within a destination.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: LocationFeatureSpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value that specifies a feature of an accommodation, represented as a property-value pair. Also called accommodation feature, amenity detail, property value specification. Examples: "hasWifi: true", "numberOfBedrooms: 3", "petsAllowed: false", "poolType: outdoor".

types.embedding_query_text: Ingredient: Any of the foods or substances that are combined to make a particular dish. Also called Component, Element, Constituent, Additive, Material. Examples: sugar, variety of flours, natural quince sourdough starter, honey.

chosen_type.label: Substance
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Ingredient' is best represented by schema.org's 'Substance', which covers matter of defined composition like sugar, flour, and salt.

candidates.label: DietarySupplement
candidates.comment: A product taken orally that contains dietary ingredients intended to supplement the diet, such as vitamins, minerals, or herbs. Also called Nutritional supplement, health supplement, vitamin, herbal remedy. Examples: Multivitamin pills, fish oil capsules, protein powder, ginseng extract. Distinct from Drug, which is primarily for treating, preventing, or diagnosing disease.

candidates.label: Substance
candidates.comment: Any matter of defined composition with discrete existence, which can be biological, mineral, or chemical. Also called material, chemical compound, element, matter. Examples: water, oxygen, penicillin, granite.

candidates.label: ChemicalSubstance
candidates.comment: A portion of matter with constant composition, composed of molecular entities of the same or different types. Also called chemical compound, chemical, substance, molecule. Examples: Water (H2O), Sodium Chloride (NaCl), Ethanol, Oxygen.

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

candidates.label: Distillery
candidates.comment: A Distillery is a FoodEstablishment that produces alcoholic beverages through distillation. Also called liquor producer, spirits manufacturer, alcohol plant. Examples: Jack Daniel's Distillery, The Macallan Distillery, Absolut Vodka Distillery. Distinct from Brewery, which produces beer through fermentation.

types.embedding_query_text: Duration: The length of time that something continues or exists. Also called Period, Span, Length of time, Term, Interval. Examples: six years.

chosen_type.label: Duration
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Duration' directly matches schema.org's 'Duration' datatype, which represents a period of time.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: ServicePeriod
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a duration for a service, often including constraints like cutoff times or business days. Also called service duration, operational window, delivery timeframe, handling period. Examples: a 2-day shipping period with a 3 PM cutoff, a 5-business-day processing time, a 24/7 support period.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

types.embedding_query_text: Hotel: An establishment providing lodging and other services for travelers. Also called Inn, Motel, Hostel, Lodging, Resort. Examples: Hotel Costes.

chosen_type.label: Hotel
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Hotel' directly matches schema.org's 'Hotel' class, which describes a lodging business.

candidates.label: Hotel
candidates.comment: A Hotel is a lodging business providing short-term, paid accommodation, typically in private rooms. Also called inn, motel, lodging establishment. Examples: Hilton Hotel, Marriott International, a boutique hotel. Distinct from Hostel, which often provides cheaper, shared dormitory-style accommodation.

candidates.label: Hostel
candidates.comment: A Hostel is a lodging business offering inexpensive accommodation, often featuring shared dormitories and communal facilities. Also called youth hostel, budget accommodation, backpacker's lodge. Examples: Generator Hostel, a local backpacker hostel, a mountain hut. Distinct from Hotel, which typically offers private rooms and more extensive services.

candidates.label: HotelRoom
candidates.comment: A HotelRoom is a specific accommodation unit within a hotel. Also called guest room, hotel suite, lodging unit. Examples: a standard double room, a king suite, a connecting room. Distinct from Room, which is a general type of accommodation that could be in any building.

candidates.label: Motel
candidates.comment: A lodging business, typically located along a highway, offering rooms with direct access from a parking area. Also called motor hotel, roadside inn, motor lodge. Examples: "Super 8 Motel", "Motel 6", a local roadside motel. Distinct from Hotel, which is generally a larger, multi-story building with interior corridors.

candidates.label: Resort
candidates.comment: A Resort is a LodgingBusiness and LocalBusiness used for relaxation or recreation, attracting visitors for holidays or vacations. Also called holiday resort, vacation resort, leisure complex. Examples: a beach resort, a ski resort, an all-inclusive resort, a spa resort.

types.embedding_query_text: Store: A retail establishment selling goods or services. Also called Shop, Market, Outlet, Retailer, Boutique. Examples: La Grande Epicerie de Paris.

chosen_type.label: Store
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Store' directly matches schema.org's 'Store' class, which describes a retail business.

candidates.label: Store
candidates.comment: A retail business that sells goods to consumers. Also called shop, retail outlet, boutique, market. Examples: a grocery store, a clothing store, an electronics store, a bookstore.

candidates.label: DepartmentStore
candidates.comment: A type of store that sells a wide variety of consumer goods across different departments. Also called Retail department store, general merchandise store. Examples: Macy's, Nordstrom, Harrods, Kohl's. Distinct from Store, which is a general category for any retail establishment.

candidates.label: OutletStore
candidates.comment: An OutletStore is a local business that sells goods, often at reduced prices, directly from a manufacturer or retailer. Also called factory outlet, discount store, clearance store. Examples: a Nike outlet, a designer brand outlet, a retail chain's clearance center. Distinct from DepartmentStore, which sells a wide range of goods at regular prices.

candidates.label: ShoeStore
candidates.comment: A retail store specializing in the sale of footwear. Also called footwear shop, shoe retailer, boot store. Examples: 'Foot Locker', 'DSW Designer Shoe Warehouse', 'Local Shoe Boutique'.

candidates.label: WholesaleStore
candidates.comment: A local business that sells goods in large quantities, typically to retailers or other businesses, rather than directly to individual consumers. Also called wholesaler, bulk store, cash and carry. Examples: Costco Business Center, a restaurant supply store, a building materials wholesaler.

types.embedding_query_text: Bread: A staple food prepared from a dough of flour and water, usually by baking. Also called Loaf, Baked good, Staple food, Roll, Bun. Examples: pain du coin, the bread of yesterday and tomorrow, famous "pain du coin".

chosen_type.label: Product
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Bread' is a specific good, which is best represented by the general schema.org 'Product' class.

mentions: the bread of yesterday and tomorrow

candidates.label: Bakery
candidates.comment: A FoodEstablishment that bakes and sells bread, cakes, and pastries. Also called bake shop, patisserie, bread shop. Examples: "The Daily Bread Bakery", "Sweet Delights Patisserie", "Grandma's Oven".

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

candidates.label: FoodService
candidates.comment: A FoodService is a Service related to providing food, such as breakfast, lunch, or dinner. Also called meal service, catering service, dining option. Examples: Breakfast service at a hotel, a school lunch program, an in-flight meal service, a catering package for an event.

candidates.label: CookAction
candidates.comment: The act of preparing or producing food through cooking processes. Also called cooking, food preparation, culinary action, baking. Examples: Baking a cake, frying an egg, grilling a steak, boiling pasta. Distinct from CreateAction, which is a broader category for making something.

candidates.label: BarOrPub
candidates.comment: A FoodEstablishment that primarily serves alcoholic beverages and often food. Also called bar, pub, tavern, lounge. Examples: "The Green Dragon Pub", "O'Malley's Bar & Grill", "The Corner Taproom". Distinct from Restaurant, which primarily focuses on serving meals.

types.embedding_query_text: Initiative: An act or strategy intended to resolve a difficulty or improve a situation. Also called Project, Program, Undertaking, Plan, Measure. Examples: anti-waste initiative.

chosen_type.label: Project
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Initiative' is explicitly listed as an alias for schema.org's 'Project' class, which describes a planned enterprise.

candidates.label: Project
candidates.comment: A Project is an Organization representing an enterprise, typically collaborative, planned to achieve a particular aim. Also called initiative, endeavor, venture. Examples: a software development project, a construction project, a research initiative, a community outreach program.

candidates.label: ResearchProject
candidates.comment: A ResearchProject is a Project representing a planned enterprise aimed at scientific or academic inquiry. Also called research initiative, study, academic project. Examples: a clinical trial, a grant-funded scientific study, a historical research project, a university-led exploration.

candidates.label: ChooseAction
candidates.comment: The act of expressing a preference or making a selection from a set of options. Also called select, pick, opt for, decide. Examples: Choosing a meal from a menu, choosing a candidate in an election, choosing a color for a car.

candidates.label: AssessAction
candidates.comment: An AssessAction is an Action involving the formation of an opinion, reaction, or sentiment about something. Also called evaluate, appraise, judge, review, rate. Examples: a critic reviewing a movie, a teacher grading an assignment, a user rating a product, a doctor evaluating a patient's condition.

candidates.label: DiscoverAction
candidates.comment: A find action representing the act of finding or uncovering an object or information. Also called Find, uncover, locate, detect, unearth. Examples: Discovering a new species, finding a lost item, uncovering a historical artifact, detecting a bug in software. Distinct from FindAction, which is a broader category for seeking something.

types.embedding_query_text: EstablishmentType: A category or classification of a business or public institution. Also called Business type, Venue category, Institution class, Sector, Classification. Examples: new venue, café, restaurant, bakery-patisserie.

chosen_type.label: BusinessEntityType
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'EstablishmentType' aligns with schema.org's 'BusinessEntityType', which describes the classification or type of a business or organization.

candidates.label: BusinessEntityType
candidates.comment: A BusinessEntityType is an Enumeration representing the legal form, size, main line of business, or position in the value chain of an organization or business person. Also called legal entity type, company structure, business classification. Examples: Corporation, Sole Proprietorship, Partnership, Non-profit Organization.

candidates.label: UKNonprofitType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of specific non-profit organization types recognized within the United Kingdom. Also called UK charity type, British non-profit category, UK voluntary sector classification. Examples: a registered charity, a community interest company (CIC), a benevolent society.

candidates.label: Restaurant
candidates.comment: A Restaurant is a FoodEstablishment and LocalBusiness serving food and drink. Also called eatery, diner, cafe. Examples: "The French Laundry", a local pizzeria, a fast-food restaurant, a fine dining establishment.

candidates.label: USNonprofitType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of specific non-profit organization types recognized within the United States. Also called US charity type, American non-profit category, US voluntary sector classification. Examples: a 501(c)(3) organization, a public charity, a private foundation.

candidates.label: Bakery
candidates.comment: A FoodEstablishment that bakes and sells bread, cakes, and pastries. Also called bake shop, patisserie, bread shop. Examples: "The Daily Bread Bakery", "Sweet Delights Patisserie", "Grandma's Oven".

candidates.label: Restaurant
candidates.comment: A Restaurant is a FoodEstablishment and LocalBusiness serving food and drink. Also called eatery, diner, cafe. Examples: "The French Laundry", a local pizzeria, a fast-food restaurant, a fine dining establishment.

candidates.label: CafeOrCoffeeShop
candidates.comment: A CafeOrCoffeeShop is a FoodEstablishment primarily serving coffee, other beverages, and often light meals or pastries. Also called coffee house, coffee bar, cafe. Examples: Starbucks, local independent coffee shop, a small bistro. Distinct from Restaurant, which typically offers a wider range of full meals.

candidates.label: BarOrPub
candidates.comment: A FoodEstablishment that primarily serves alcoholic beverages and often food. Also called bar, pub, tavern, lounge. Examples: "The Green Dragon Pub", "O'Malley's Bar & Grill", "The Corner Taproom". Distinct from Restaurant, which primarily focuses on serving meals.

candidates.label: FoodEstablishment
candidates.comment: A FoodEstablishment is a LocalBusiness primarily involved in food-related services. Also called eatery, restaurant, food service provider. Examples: A restaurant, a cafe, a bakery, a catering company.
